questions.question: In 1908 Khudiram Bose along with ______ was involved in throwing a bomb at a carriage believing it to be occupied by Kingsford, the then sitting judge of Muzaffarpur.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Prafulla Chaki.
Prafulla Chaki was an Indian revolutionary associated with the Jugantar group. Khudiram Bose was among the youngest martyrs of India's freedom struggle. He was executed on August 11, 1908, in Muzaffarpur jail in Bihar.

questions.question: During British rule in India, who among the following unfurled the flag of India in Germany in 1907?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bhikaji Cama.
Madam Bhikaji Cama unfurled the first version of the Indian national flag in Stuttgart, Germany in 1907. She founded the 'Paris Indian Society'.
  • Annie Besant (British socialist) founded the Home Rule League in India and was the first woman president of INC.
  • Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman president of INC.
  • Sucheta Kriplani was India's first female Chief Minister (Uttar Pradesh).

questions.question: Who among the following revolutionaries was one of the co-founders of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) which got established in 1928 at Ferozeshah Kotla in Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bhagat Singh.
The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA), formerly known as the Hindustan Republican Army (HRA), was founded by Ram Prasad Bismil, Sachindra Nath Bakshi, Sachindranath Sanyal, and Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee. HRA was established in October 1924 in Kanpur. Bhagat Singh was one of the co-founders when HRA took on socialist ideas under Chandrashekhar Azad's leadership in 1928.

questions.question:
Match the following leaders with the related years:
List I (Events/Positions)List II (Years)
A. Khudai Khidmatgars1. 1929
B. First Law Minister2. 1947
C. Forward Bloc3. 1939
D. Non-Cooperation Movement4. 1920
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4.
  • Khudai Khidmatgars was founded in 1929 by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Frontier Gandhi).
  • First Law Minister of India was Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in 1947.
  • Forward Bloc was founded in 1939 by Subhas Chandra Bose.
  • Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in 1920 by Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.question: The 'Servants of India Society' was the brainchild of which of the following leaders?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gopal Krishna Gokhale.
Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905. He also founded the Ranade Institute of Economics (1908) and started an English weekly newspaper, 'The Hitavada' (The people's paper).

questions.question: On 8th April 1929, who among the following two revolutionists threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly?
questions.option_2: Bhagat Singh and Ram Prasad Bismil
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt.
On 8th April 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly against the passage of the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill. They were members of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association. Bhagat Singh was hanged on 23rd March 1931 in Lahore jail at the age of 23.

questions.question: Who is regarded as the Mother of Indian Revolution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Madame Cama.
Madame Bhikaji Cama is regarded as the 'Mother of Indian Revolution'. She is famous for hosting the precursor to the Indian National Flag on foreign soil in Stuttgart, Germany in 1907.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Lala Lajpat Rai died due to injuries sustained during the Anti-Simon Commission protest in 1928.
Reason (R): The Simon Commission, sent to India in 1928, included Indian members to represent the people's voices.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A is true, but R is false.
  • Assertion (A) is true: Lala Lajpat Rai (also called 'Punjab Kesari' and 'Lion of Punjab') died due to injuries sustained during a lathi charge while leading an Anti-Simon Commission protest in 1928.
  • Reason (R) is false: The Simon Commission had no Indian members (it was all-British), which was the primary reason for the protests.

questions.question: Who among the following, along with her close associates, started the secret congress radio during the Quit India Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Usha Mehta.
Usha Mehta, along with her close associates, started the secret Congress Radio during the Quit India Movement. She was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 1998.

questions.question: The statement 'We shall die to awaken the nation' was made by
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bagha Jatin.
Bagha Jatin (Jatindranath Mukherjee) was born on 7th December 1879 in Kayagram (Nadia district), present-day Bangladesh. He acquired the moniker 'Bagha Jatin' when he single-handedly killed a Bengal tiger in 1906. The statement 'We shall die to awaken the nation' is attributed to him.

questions.question: Which freedom fighter was involved in the Kakori Train Action in 1925, for which the British government condemned him to death?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ram Prasad Bismil.
The Kakori Train Action (Kakori Conspiracy) was a train robbery that took place on 9 August 1925 near Lucknow, organized by the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA). Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, and Roshan Singh were hanged on 19 December 1927 for their involvement.

questions.question: The Revolutionary Socialist Party was established in
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1940.
The Revolutionary Socialist Party (RSP) was established on 19 March 1940 by Tridib Chaudhuri. It has its roots in the Bengali liberation movement Anushilan Samiti and the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association. The first general secretary of the party was Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about famous patriotic slogans:
1. The words 'Sarfaroshi ki tamanna ab hamare dil me hai, dekha hai zor kitna baazu-e-qaatil mein hai' were composed by Ramprasad Bismil.
2. The slogan 'Tum Mujhe Khoon Do, Mai Tumhe Azadi Dunga' is associated with Bhagat Singh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 only.
  • Statement 1 is correct: The famous poem 'Sarfaroshi ki tamanna' was composed by Ramprasad Bismil.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: 'Tum Mujhe Khoon Do, Mai Tumhe Azadi Dunga' was said by Subhas Chandra Bose, not Bhagat Singh.
Other slogans: Mahatma Gandhi - 'Karo ya Maro'; Muhammad Iqbal - 'Sare Jahan Se Achha'; Bankim Chandra Chatterjee - 'Vande Mataram'.

questions.question: Which of the following revolutionaries stated during his trial that 'he did not wish to glorify the cult of the bomb and pistol but wanted a revolution in society'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bhagat Singh.
Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929. During his trial, Bhagat Singh stated that he did not wish to glorify the cult of the bomb and pistol but wanted a revolution in society.

questions.question: Who among the following revolutionaries was associated with Swadesh Bandhav Samiti?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ashwini Kumar Dutta.
Ashwini Kumar Dutta founded the Swadesh Bandhab Samiti on 6th August 1905 in Barisal district (Bangladesh). He also published the weekly paper 'Barisal Hitaishi' and was responsible for the creation of the Cooperative Hindustan Bank in 1908.

questions.question: Who among the following organized the armed rebellion against the British Raj in 1879 in Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Vasudev Balwant Phadke.
Vasudev Balwant Phadke is known as the 'First Revolutionary' and also the 'Father of militant nationalism in India.' He organized an armed rebellion against the British Raj in 1879 in Maharashtra.

questions.question: The Communist Party of India was founded at ______ in October 1920.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Tashkent.
M.N. Roy (Manabendra Nath Roy) and Abani Mukherji founded the Communist Party of India (CPI) in 1920 in Tashkent (now the capital of Uzbekistan). The Communist Party of India was officially formed in 1925 in Kanpur.

questions.question: The Koraput Revolution occurred in ______ during the Quit India Movement.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Orissa.
The Koraput Revolution occurred in Odisha (Orissa) during the Quit India Movement. On August 25, 1942, 19 people died on the spot in police firing at Paparandi in Nabarangpur (Odisha). More than a thousand were jailed in Koraput district.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Bharat Naujawan Sabha is INCORRECT?
questions.option_2: Bhagat Singh became its founding secretary
questions.option_4: It started political work among the youth, peasants, and workers
questions.solution:
The correct answer is It was established in 1927.
Bharat Naujawan Sabha was founded in Lahore (Punjab) in 1926 (not 1927) by Bhagat Singh, who became its founding secretary. It started political work among youth, peasants, and workers. Therefore, statement 3 is incorrect.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Indigo Revolt in Bengal began as a non-violent strike in 1859 when ryots refused to cultivate indigo.
Reason (R): The Indigo Revolt was led by Bishnu Charan Biswas and Digambar Biswas of Nadia district, Bengal.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false.
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
  • Assertion (A) is true: The Indigo Revolt began as a non-violent strike in March 1859 when ryots refused to cultivate indigo.
  • Reason (R) is true: The revolt was led by Digambar Biswas and Bishnu Biswas of Nadia district, Bengal.
  • However, R describes who led the revolt but does not explain why it began as a non-violent strike.

questions.question: Which of the following revolutionaries was arrested by the British as an accused in the Alipore Bomb Conspiracy Case?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kanaill Dutta.
Kanaill Dutta was among the 33 revolutionaries arrested in the Emperor vs Aurobindo Ghosh (Alipore Bomb Case). The Alipore Bomb case was a historic trial in which the British Government tried to implicate Sri Aurobindo in various revolutionary activities.

questions.question: At which of the following jails was Khudiram Bose sent to the gallows?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Muzaffarpur.
Khudiram Bose was arrested for trying to assassinate British judge Douglas Kingsford. He was executed on August 11, 1908, in Muzaffarpur jail in Bihar.

questions.question: Who among the following persons was associated with the Chittagong Armoury Raid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ardhendu Dastidar.
Ardhendu Dastidar was associated with the Chittagong Armoury Raid led by Surya Sen in 1930.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and its aftermath:
Statement 1: Michael O'Dwyer, responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, was assassinated in Caxton Hall, London.
Statement 2: Udham Singh carried out the assassination in 1940 as an act of revenge for the massacre.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is incorrect, Statement 2 is correct
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both statements are correct.
  • Statement 1 is correct: Michael O'Dwyer, who was responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, was assassinated in Caxton Hall, London.
  • Statement 2 is correct: Udham Singh carried out the assassination in 1940 as an act of revenge for the massacre.

questions.question: Who among the following assassinated Sir William Hutt Curzon Wyllie in London?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Madan Lal Dhingra.
Madan Lal Dhingra was an Indian revolutionary independence activist. While studying in England, he assassinated Sir William Hutt Curzon Wyllie, a British official, cited as one of the first acts of revolution in the Indian independence movement in the 20th century.
